source.heading: PASSAGE IV
source.directions: The passage below has gaps numbered 16 to 25. Immediately following each gap, four options are provided. Choose the most appropriate options for each gap. Each question carries 3 marks

passage.text: The medical definition of miscarriage is the spontaneous loss of a pregnancy before twenty-four weeks.
Miscarriage is very common, occurring in ten to twenty per cent, of conformed pregnancies.
Most of these feature {{16}} twelve week of pregnancy.
The most common {{17}} is vaginal bleeding, which can range from light spotting to heavier than a period.
You may see blood clots, brown discharge or other tissues that are not {{18}} identifiable.
Sometimes a sac-like structure is seen.
Often, there is cramping with pelvic or back pain.
You may find that the usual symptoms of pregnancy, such as breast tenderness, feeling sick and having to pass urine more {{19}} than usual stop unexpectedly.
Sometimes there are no signs or symptoms of miscarriage and pregnancy symptoms continue, and the miscarriage is only {{20}} in a routine scan.
About half of all early miscarriages happen because of a problem in the way the genetic material from the egg and sperm have combined during {{21}}.
It can be difficult to find out why this has {{22}}, but it is more likely to be due to random chance than to any underlying problem with either parent.
Imbalances in pregnancy hormones, problems in the immune {{23}}, and some serious infections are also thought to make miscarriages more likely.
The risk of miscarriage {{24}} with age because the quality of eggs deteriorates.
If a woman drinks too much alcohol or smokes heavily, the risk of miscarriage is higher.
It is also increased with {{25}} pregnancies such as twins.

questions.stem: Most of these feature ...16... twelve week of pregnancy.

options.why: Penultimate means next to last. The paragraph is describing the early weeks.
The phrase identifies the first twelve weeks rather than one particular week.
Around suggests an approximate point. The phrase refers to the whole early period.
For would tell how long something lasts. The gap asks when it happens.

questions.stem: The most common ...17... is vaginal bleeding, which can range from light spotting to heavier than a period.

options.why: Bleeding is an indication in this sentence, not a category of miscarriage.
The text names a sign a person might notice, not what causes the event.
Period refers to a time span or to menstruation. The sentence singles out a sign.
Bleeding is the sign the sentence describes. Symptom is the word for that sign.

questions.clue: The most common … is vaginal bleeding

questions.stem: You may see blood clots, brown discharge or other tissues that are not ...18... identifiable.

options.why: Clearly identifiable means easy to recognise. That fits a description of what a person may see.
Naturally does not say whether the tissue can be recognised easily.
Directly implies a particular method of identifying something. No method is given.
The sentence describes what a person may see. It gives no clinical test or diagnosis.

questions.clue: other tissues that are not … identifiable

questions.stem: You may find that the usual symptoms of pregnancy, such as breast tenderness, feeling sick and having to pass urine more ...19... than usual stop unexpectedly.

options.why: The phrase contrasts how often something happens, rather than how painful it is.
More frequently than usual compares how often someone needs to pass urine.
Gradually tells how slowly a change happens. It does not give the needed frequency.
Commonly describes how widespread something is. Frequently fits how often an individual does it.

questions.clue: having to pass urine more … than usual

questions.stem: Sometimes there are no signs or symptoms of miscarriage and pregnancy symptoms continue, and the miscarriage is only ...20... in a routine scan.

options.why: A scan can reveal what has happened. It does not prevent the event in this sentence.
Managed would imply treatment. The clue is that there were no obvious signs.
The scan is how the event becomes known when there are no visible signs.
The sentence describes detection. It does not say the scan stops the event.

questions.clue: no signs or symptoms … only … in a routine scan

questions.stem: About half of all early miscarriages happen because of a problem in the way the genetic material from the egg and sperm have combined during ...21....

options.why: Pregnancy names the broader period, not the event in which the egg and sperm combine.
Incubation does not name the combination of the egg and sperm.
Mating does not name the joining described in the sentence.
Fertilization names the event in which the egg and sperm combine.

questions.clue: genetic material from the egg and sperm have combined during …

questions.stem: It can be difficult to find out why this has ...22..., but it is more likely to be due to random chance than to any underlying problem with either parent.

options.why: Occurred means happened. The sentence asks why the event happened.
The sentence is not about something becoming larger.
The sentence asks why the event happened, not why it kept happening.
Emerged often means came into view or became known. The sentence asks for the cause of the event.

questions.clue: find out why this has … but it is more likely to be due to random chance

questions.stem: Imbalances in pregnancy hormones, problems in the immune ...23..., and some serious infections are also thought to make miscarriages more likely.

options.why: Syndrome is a group of symptoms. It does not name the body's defence system.
Immune process is too vague for the part of the body meant here.
An immune response is a reaction. The sentence refers to a wider system in which problems may occur.
Immune system is the usual name for the body's defences.

questions.stem: The risk of miscarriage ...24... with age because the quality of eggs deteriorates.

options.why: Deteriorates means becomes worse. The sentence links that worsening with a higher risk.
The risk exists already. The sentence describes a change with age.
Reduces means becomes lower, which goes against the reason given.
Appears would mean the risk begins to show. The sentence is about its level changing.

questions.clue: with age because the quality of eggs deteriorates

questions.stem: It is also increased with ...25... pregnancies such as twins.

options.why: Twins are given as an example of more than one baby, rather than of every complication.
Advance does not describe the number of babies in the example.
Twins are an example of a pregnancy with more than one baby.
Confirmed tells whether a pregnancy is established. It does not explain the example of twins.
